title: Finite models for finite constant sheaves
statement: Let X be a scheme, Lambda a commutative ring, and F a constant sheaf of Lambda-modules on the small etale site of X [def-constructible-constant]. If F has finitely generated geometric stalks [def-constructible-finite], there is a finitely generated Lambda-module M and an isomorphism F ≅ M_X. This includes the empty scheme.

source.place: IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf.ihom_unit docstring, local finite presentation argument

proof.text: If X is empty, Etale.isZero_sheaf_of_isEmpty makes F and the constant sheaf at the zero module zero. Their unique isomorphism gives the model; the zero module is finitely generated.
Otherwise choose x in X and the geometric point s with field SeparableClosure κ(x). Constancy supplies M and F ≅ M_X using Sheaf.mem_essImage_of_isConstant.

The functor sheafFiber maps this isomorphism to an isomorphism on stalks. Compose with Point.sheafFiberConstantSheafIso M to identify F_s with M, then transport finite generation using ConcreteCategory.IsFinitelyGenerated.of_iso and ModuleCat.isFinitelyGenerated_iff.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_constant_model
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hc : F.IsConstant X.smallEtaleTopology) (hf : IsFiniteSheaf F) :
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ, Module.Finite Λ M ∧
      Nonempty (F ≅ (constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M)
